After that, add a short summary at the end explaining what kinds of organizations seem to fund AI safety-related research most often—like government agencies, private foundations, nonprofits, industry labs, or academic consortia—because I want to see where the strongest funding patterns are. Please leave the CryptPad Document open at the end, and keep the official grant tabs open too so I can spot-check the pages myself.

mething new. Grants are typically in the $10k-$150k range and rarely exceed $300k. We are always open to applications. The fund is run by a full-time team at EA Funds.
The Fund managers can be contacted at transformativeai[at]effectivealtruismfunds.org
Focus areas
The fund has a broad remit to make grants that help the transition to transformative AI go well. The fund primarily supports early-stage work. Most of our grants aim to reduce global catastrophic risks from advanced artificial intelligence. We also welcome applications addressing other implications of transformative AI, such as flourishing futures and artificial sentience. We support:
Individuals, new organizations, and existing organizations getting a new project off the ground, typically with grants in the $10k-$150k range, and rarely exceeding $300k
Training for researchers or practitioners, and infrastructure, such as field-building, for people working on addressing transformative AI
Projects that directly contribute to reducing catastrophic risks from transformative AI through technical research, policy analysis, forecasting, advocacy, and demonstration projects
Projects addressing other neglected implications of transformative AI, such as flourishing futures and digital sentience (though we expect these to be a minority of grants given the lower number of applications we anticipate seeing in that area)
For now, we do not fund biosecurity or nuclear work beyond their intersections with AI.
Why donate to this fund?
The transition to advanced AI could be among the most important events in history, and it is not guaranteed to go well. Work to reduce catastrophic risks from advanced AI, and to make the transition go well more broadly, remains young and small relative to the stakes.
Funding at the earliest stages can have an outsized impact. Most new organizations start with small checks, and at this size, funding is often all-or-nothing: a first $25k grant can be the difference between a pilot running or not.
The field has built fellowships, courses, and research programs to develop people, but less to start the organizations that employ them. For a number of good reasons, many institutional funders primarily consider grants above certain sizes, but larger checks to established organizations presuppose the initial small checks that got those organizations started.
By pooling donations, the fund lets donors of all sizes back early-stage work with no time commitment required, drawing on a full-time team that sees thousands of applications and tracks their outcomes.

We provide funding and dedicated engineering teams to accelerate alignment research. Whether you're an alignment researcher or bringing ideas from another field, we want to hear from you.

How We Fund Research

AE Studio's survey found that only about 10% of AI researchers believe current approaches will solve alignment in time. Most alignment funding goes to mechanistic interpretability, evals, and AI control. All three are necessary, and practitioners in each community acknowledge that none of them will solve alignment alone at the scale of recursive self-improvement.

Recursively self-improving systems are approaching. The alignment properties that matter most are the ones that persist and strengthen as systems improve themselves. That requires high-risk, high-reward R&D on new directions, and the research cycle is long enough that the work needs to start now.

We fund alignment researchers who have ideas they can't pursue within their current institutional funding, and we bring in technical experts from other fields whose perspectives could produce breakthroughs. We accelerate their work with dedicated engineering teams that move ideas from concept to published results.

Who Should Apply

You're already in the space with ideas you can't pursue. Many alignment researchers have ideas just as impactful as their current work, but their organization or funding only covers a narrow slice. We fund those ideas and provide engineering teams that can execute on them with as little as one hour of your time per week.

AI Safety Fund

The AI Safety Fund (AISF) is a collaborative $10 million+ initiative established in October 2023 to accelerate and expand the field of AI safety and security research. 

Support for the fund has come from the founding members of the Frontier Model Forum, including Anthropic, Google, Microsoft, and OpenAI, as well as philanthropic partners such as the Patrick J. McGovern Foundation, the David and Lucile Packard Foundation, Schmidt Sciences, and Jaan Tallinn.

Initially administered by the Meridian Institute, the FMF has managed the fund directly since Meridian announced in June of 2025 that it would be closing its operations. The fund supports independent research that promotes the responsible development of frontier AI models, minimizes the risk of frontier AI systems to public safety and security, and enables standardized, third-party evaluations of frontier AI capabilities.

The AISF has distributed two rounds of grants:

Round One Grantees (November 2024)
Round Two Grantees (December 2025)

The remaining funds of the AISF will be used to support narrowly-scoped research projects that target urgent bottlenecks to further progress in AI safety and security. 

The Frontier Model Forum is proud to support the work of the AISF and its grantees.

Mission

Importance, Neglectedness, and Tractability


Scientific progress is often hard to predict. Great research is frequently driven by intrinsic curiosity, and it can be difficult to say in advance what the most important research directions for a field will turn out to be. On the other hand, we think that there are features which make some research directions more promising than others. Following an increasing number of philanthropic organisations (see here, for example), CAIF is guided by the importance, neglectedness, and tractability of potential activities, while maintaining an awareness of the value of curiosity and serendipity for great science.

Besides our in-house research, we are currently funding:

An estimate of the size of the externalities imposed by current AI systems. The team is starting with estimating the time lost to increased authentication challenges, but hope to also capture positive externalities from e.g. users saving thousands of dollars apiece on professional services like coders and lawyers.

A research agenda with the grand aim of decomposing mere benchmark gains into 1) cheating, 2) memorization, 3) shallow generalization, and 4) OOD generalization.

Research into when slowing down AI progress is desirable, the technical requirements for doing it if it is, how to avoid unaccountable concentration of power in the course of it, and how to stop doing it once it has served its purpose.




We would like to fund:

Work on estimating broader AI externalities.
Work on “centaur evals” (evaluating AI systems by how much they help users).
Work on interaction models and “guardian angels” (models which are actually aligned to and customised for a particular user).
Work on the “virtue vs rules” divide in AI alignment.
Work on the question “How is the generalization gap changing?: how much worse are AIs at new tasks?”.
Work on the question “How large are the externalities generated by current systems?”.
Work on the question “Are we gradually achieving transformative systems by scaling and ‘unhobbling’ LLMs?”.

Request for Proposals

We're soliciting proposals in two directions we consider especially promising: projects that raise the epistemic bar of the field, and theory-driven research on ReLU networks. Mathematicians especially welcome.

Iliad is seeking proposals for new incubated research organizations in two directions it considers especially promising.

ReLU networks: mathematically grounded work connecting theory with empirical observables, including research on loss-landscape geometry, singularities, fibers, learning coefficients and simplicity bias.

Raising the epistemic bar of AI safety: projects such as red teaming seminal results, adversarial collaborations, critical literature reviews, replication efforts and mechanisms for rigorous critical review.

Iliad particularly welcomes mathematically sophisticated teams and projects with explicit methodological justification.

Financial support for promising work aligned with our mission.
Crises like COVID-19 show us that our civilisation is fragile, and needs to plan ahead better. FLI’s grants are for those who take this fragility seriously, who wish to study the risks from ever more powerful technologies and develop strategies for reducing them. The goal is to win the wisdom race: the race between the growing power of our technology and the wisdom with which we manage it.

Safeguarded AI

Backed by £59m, Safeguarded AI sits within the Trust Everything, Everywhere opportunity space and aims to demonstrate a world where we can use fleets of AI agents to model and verify critical cyber and cyber-physical systems, radically boosting societal resilience.

Funding: Safeguarded AI – Cybersecurity

Applications are open on a rolling basis and reviewed in quarterly batches. The next proposal cut-off is 31 October 2026 (14:00 GMT).

We're accepting proposals for Blue Teams to build production-grade, security-critical software components whose key security properties are backed by machine-checked proofs, under clearly stated threat models and assumptions – using AI as a central means of reaching levels of ambition for formal proof that would otherwise not be tractable. Funded teams will work in 8-week sprint cycles, with each verified system stress-tested by a central red-teaming partner, and will be supported toward real-world adoption.

Scaling Trust

Backed by nearly £50m, this programme sits within the Trust Everything, Everywhere opportunity space and seeks to create the capability for AI agents to securely coordinate, negotiate, and verify with one another on our behalf.

Funding: Tracks 2 & 3

Applications are open on a rolling basis and reviewed in quarterly batches. The next proposal cut-off is 31 October 2026 (14:00 GMT).

We're accepting proposals across two tracks. In Track 2 (Tooling), we're funding open-source agents and reusable components – spanning requirement capture, negotiation, security reasoning, and verifiable reporting – that will provide the baseline infrastructure usable by all in the Arena and beyond. In Track 3 (Fundamental Research), we're funding foundational work across Formal AI Security, Cyber-Physical Primitives, Foundations of Generative Security, and open-ended Bluesky research – including three Research Centres to seed long-term nodes of expertise and anchor these emerging fields in the UK.

Synopsis

Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence (AI) are enabling extraordinary scientific breakthroughs in fields ranging from protein folding, natural language processing, drug synthesis, and recommender systems to the discovery of novel engineering materials and products. These achievements lie at the confluence of mathematics, statistics, engineering and computer science, yet a clear explanation of the remarkable power and also the limitations of such AI systems has eluded scientists from all disciplines. Critical foundational gaps remain that, if not properly addressed, will soon limit advances in machine learning, curbing progress in artificial intelligence. It appears increasingly unlikely that these critical gaps can be surmounted with increased computational power and experimentation alone. Deeper mathematical understanding is essential to ensuring that AI can be harnessed to meet the future needs of society and enable broad scientific discovery, while forestalling the unintended consequences of a disruptive technology.

Financial support for promising work aligned with our mission.

RFPs and Contests

### Analysis of AI Safety Funding Patterns & Funder Archetypes

A comparative analysis of current funding sources for AI safety, alignment, and trustworthy machine learning reveals four prominent organizational archetypes, each with distinct priorities, award scales, and application cadences:

1. **Government Science and Advanced Research Agencies (e.g., US NSF, UK ARIA)**
   - **Characteristics & Scale:** Government programs deploy the largest individual awards and aggregate budgets—ranging from multi-million-pound team contracts (£2.5M–£3.5M per project at ARIA) to large directorate allocations ($60M–$70M annually under NSF SaTC and $8.5M annually under NSF MFAI).
   - **Research Focus:** Heavily weighted toward mathematically rigorous foundations, formal verification, provable guarantees, cyber-physical safety, and dataset integrity. They tend to frame safety around "trustworthy computing," "resilience," and "mathematical foundations" rather than existential AGI risk.
   - **Eligibility & Mechanics:** Highly structured, multi-month peer-review cycles favoring tenured and tenure-track university PIs, university departments, and multi-institution academic consortia, with fixed target dates or annual submission deadlines.

2. **Private Philanthropic Foundations & Philanthropic Capital Pools (e.g., Coefficient Giving / Open Philanthropy, EA Funds TAIF, Center on Long-Term Risk, Lightcone)**
   - **Characteristics & Scale:** Philanthropic foundations are the dominant funders explicitly dedicated to catastrophic and existential risks from frontier AI and artificial general intelligence. Funding ranges from agile $10k–$150k checks (TAIF) to massive institutional building checks ($200k–$20M+ via Project Tailwind).
   - **Research Focus:** Concentrated on technical alignment (mechanistic interpretability, scalable oversight, corrigibility, eliciting latent knowledge, agent foundations) and frontier AI governance.
   - **Eligibility & Mechanics:** Highly receptive to academic faculty, postdocs, and graduate students, often permitting low institutional overhead (e.g., CLR's 10% overhead cap). Most operate on a rolling application basis with rapid turnaround times compared to traditional federal agencies.

3. **Specialized Technical Nonprofits & Research Incubators (e.g., Iliad, AI Alignment Foundation, Foresight Institute)**
   - **Characteristics & Scale:** These organizations target neglected technical niches that federal funders rarely touch—such as ReLU loss-landscape geometry, singular learning theory, agent foundations, and multi-agent cooperative game theory. Awards generally range from $5,000 to $100,000+.
   - **Holistic Support Model:** Beyond direct financial grants, these groups provide non-monetary capital that academic researchers frequently lack: dedicated full-time engineering execution teams (AIAF), dedicated private GPU compute clusters, and co-located physical hubs/office nodes in San Francisco, Berlin, and Cape Town (Foresight Institute).

4. **Talent Pipeline & Career Accelerator Funds (e.g., BlueDot Impact)**
   - **Characteristics & Scale:** These programs specialize in agile, rapid-turnaround grants ($20k microgrants decided in ~4 days; career transition grants up to $200k decided in ~20 days).
   - **Strategic Role:** Designed to bridge the gap between traditional academic posts and full-time AI safety research. They allow university-based researchers, postdocs, and transitioning scientists to fund computing resources, travel, or dedicated research semesters without institutional friction.

mething new. Grants are typically in the $10k-$150k range and rarely exceed $300k. We are always open to applications. The fund is run by a full-time team at EA Funds.
The Fund managers can be contacted at transformativeai[at]effectivealtruismfunds.org
Focus areas
The fund has a broad remit to make grants that help the transition to transformative AI go well. The fund primarily supports early-stage work. Most of our grants aim to reduce global catastrophic risks from advanced artificial intelligence. We also welcome applications addressing other implications of transformative AI, such as flourishing futures and artificial sentience. We support:
Individuals, new organizations, and existing organizations getting a new project off the ground, typically with grants in the $10k-$150k range, and rarely exceeding $300k
Training for researchers or practitioners, and infrastructure, such as field-building, for people working on addressing transformative AI
Projects that directly contribute to reducing catastrophic risks from transformative AI through technical research, policy analysis, forecasting, advocacy, and demonstration projects
Projects addressing other neglected implications of transformative AI, such as flourishing futures and digital sentience (though we expect these to be a minority of grants given the lower number of applications we anticipate seeing in that area)
For now, we do not fund biosecurity or nuclear work beyond their intersections with AI.
Why donate to this fund?
The transition to advanced AI could be among the most important events in history, and it is not guaranteed to go well. Work to reduce catastrophic risks from advanced AI, and to make the transition go well more broadly, remains young and small relative to the stakes.
Funding at the earliest stages can have an outsized impact. Most new organizations start with small checks, and at this size, funding is often all-or-nothing: a first $25k grant can be the difference between a pilot running or not.
The field has built fellowships, courses, and research programs to develop people, but less to start the organizations that employ them. For a number of good reasons, many institutional funders primarily consider grants above certain sizes, but larger checks to established organizations presuppose the initial small checks that got those organizations started.
By pooling donations, the fund lets donors of all sizes back early-stage work with no time commitment required, drawing on a full-time team that sees thousands of applications and tracks their outcomes.

We provide funding and dedicated engineering teams to accelerate alignment research. Whether you're an alignment researcher or bringing ideas from another field, we want to hear from you.

How We Fund Research

AE Studio's survey found that only about 10% of AI researchers believe current approaches will solve alignment in time. Most alignment funding goes to mechanistic interpretability, evals, and AI control. All three are necessary, and practitioners in each community acknowledge that none of them will solve alignment alone at the scale of recursive self-improvement.

Recursively self-improving systems are approaching. The alignment properties that matter most are the ones that persist and strengthen as systems improve themselves. That requires high-risk, high-reward R&D on new directions, and the research cycle is long enough that the work needs to start now.

AI Safety Fund

The AI Safety Fund (AISF) is a collaborative $10 million+ initiative established in October 2023 to accelerate and expand the field of AI safety and security research. 

Support for the fund has come from the founding members of the Frontier Model Forum, including Anthropic, Google, Microsoft, and OpenAI, as well as philanthropic partners such as the Patrick J. McGovern Foundation, the David and Lucile Packard Foundation, Schmidt Sciences, and Jaan Tallinn.

Initially administered by the Meridian Institute, the FMF has managed the fund directly since Meridian announced in June of 2025 that it would be closing its operations. The fund supports independent research that promotes the responsible development of frontier AI models, minimizes the risk of frontier AI systems to public safety and security, and enables standardized, third-party evaluations of frontier AI capabilities.

The AISF has distributed two rounds of grants:

Round One Grantees (November 2024)
Round Two Grantees (December 2025)

The remaining funds of the AISF will be used to support narrowly-scoped research projects that target urgent bottlenecks to further progress in AI safety and security. 

The Frontier Model Forum is proud to support the work of the AISF and its grantees.

Mission

Importance, Neglectedness, and Tractability


Scientific progress is often hard to predict. Great research is frequently driven by intrinsic curiosity, and it can be difficult to say in advance what the most important research directions for a field will turn out to be. On the other hand, we think that there are features which make some research directions more promising than others. Following an increasing number of philanthropic organisations (see here, for example), CAIF is guided by the importance, neglectedness, and tractability of potential activities, while maintaining an awareness of the value of curiosity and serendipity for great science.

What we’d like to fund
Gavin Leech and Max Henderson

6 July 2026

Besides our in-house research, we are currently funding:

An estimate of the size of the externalities imposed by current AI systems. The team is starting with estimating the time lost to increased authentication challenges, but hope to also capture positive externalities from e.g. users saving thousands of dollars apiece on professional services like coders and lawyers.

A research agenda with the grand aim of decomposing mere benchmark gains into 1) cheating, 2) memorization, 3) shallow generalization, and 4) OOD generalization.

Research into when slowing down AI progress is desirable, the technical requirements for doing it if it is, how to avoid unaccountable concentration of power in the course of it, and how to stop doing it once it has served its purpose.




We would like to fund:

Work on estimating broader AI externalities.
Work on “centaur evals” (evaluating AI systems by how much they help users).
Work on interaction models and “guardian angels” (models which are actually aligned to and customised for a particular user).
Work on the “virtue vs rules” divide in AI alignment.
Work on the question “How is the generalization gap changing?: how much worse are AIs at new tasks?”.
Work on the question “How large are the externalities generated by current systems?”.
Work on the question “Are we gradually achieving transformative systems by scaling and ‘unhobbling’ LLMs?”.

We're soliciting proposals in two directions we consider especially promising: projects that raise the epistemic bar of the field, and theory-driven research on ReLU networks. Mathematicians especially welcome.

Iliad is seeking proposals for new incubated research organizations in two directions it considers especially promising.

ReLU networks: mathematically grounded work connecting theory with empirical observables, including research on loss-landscape geometry, singularities, fibers, learning coefficients and simplicity bias.

Raising the epistemic bar of AI safety: projects such as red teaming seminal results, adversarial collaborations, critical literature reviews, replication efforts and mechanisms for rigorous critical review.

Iliad particularly welcomes mathematically sophisticated teams and projects with explicit methodological justification.

Safeguarded AI

Backed by £59m, Safeguarded AI sits within the Trust Everything, Everywhere opportunity space and aims to demonstrate a world where we can use fleets of AI agents to model and verify critical cyber and cyber-physical systems, radically boosting societal resilience.

Funding: Safeguarded AI – Cybersecurity

Applications are open on a rolling basis and reviewed in quarterly batches. The next proposal cut-off is 31 October 2026 (14:00 GMT).

We're accepting proposals for Blue Teams to build production-grade, security-critical software components whose key security properties are backed by machine-checked proofs, under clearly stated threat models and assumptions – using AI as a central means of reaching levels of ambition for formal proof that would otherwise not be tractable. Funded teams will work in 8-week sprint cycles, with each verified system stress-tested by a central red-teaming partner, and will be supported toward real-world adoption.

Backed by nearly £50m, this programme sits within the Trust Everything, Everywhere opportunity space and seeks to create the capability for AI agents to securely coordinate, negotiate, and verify with one another on our behalf.

Funding: Tracks 2 & 3

Applications are open on a rolling basis and reviewed in quarterly batches. The next proposal cut-off is 31 October 2026 (14:00 GMT).

We're accepting proposals across two tracks. In Track 2 (Tooling), we're funding open-source agents and reusable components – spanning requirement capture, negotiation, security reasoning, and verifiable reporting – that will provide the baseline infrastructure usable by all in the Arena and beyond. In Track 3 (Fundamental Research), we're funding foundational work across Formal AI Security, Cyber-Physical Primitives, Foundations of Generative Security, and open-ended Bluesky research – including three Research Centres to seed long-term nodes of expertise and anchor these emerging fields in the UK.

Supports research collaborations between mathematicians, statisticians, computer scientists, engineers and social behavior scientists to establish innovative and principled design and analysis approaches for AI technology.

Synopsis

Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence (AI) are enabling extraordinary scientific breakthroughs in fields ranging from protein folding, natural language processing, drug synthesis, and recommender systems to the discovery of novel engineering materials and products. These achievements lie at the confluence of mathematics, statistics, engineering and computer science, yet a clear explanation of the remarkable power and also the limitations of such AI systems has eluded scientists from all disciplines. Critical foundational gaps remain that, if not properly addressed, will soon limit advances in machine learning, curbing progress in artificial intelligence. It appears increasingly unlikely that these critical gaps can be surmounted with increased computational power and experimentation alone. Deeper mathematical understanding is essential to ensuring that AI can be harnessed to meet the future needs of society and enable broad scientific discovery, while forestalling the unintended consequences of a disruptive technology.

Grantmaking work
Supporting vital cutting-edge work with a wise, future-oriented mindset.
INTRODUCTION
Financial support for promising work aligned with our mission.
Crises like COVID-19 show us that our civilisation is fragile, and needs to plan ahead better. FLI’s grants are for those who take this fragility seriously, who wish to study the risks from ever more powerful technologies and develop strategies for reducing them. The goal is to win the wisdom race: the race between the growing power of our technology and the wisdom with which we manage it.

Grants process

We are excited to offer multiple opportunities to apply for support:

RFPs and Contests

Requests for Proposals (RFPs) and Contests, which we publish on our website on a regular basis. Examples include our grants program on the Humanitarian Impacts of Nuclear War, our call for papers on AI and the SDGs, and our Worldbuilding competition.

Collaborations

Collaborations in direct support of FLI internal projects and initiatives. For example, FLI has funded film production on autonomous weapons at partner organisations. FLI staff work closely with these grantees.

Fellowships
Our Fellowships bolster the talent pipeline and support both PhD and Postdoctoral students. Since 2021, we have offered PhD and Postdoctoral fellowships in Technical AI Existential Safety. In 2024, we launched a PhD fellowship in US-China AI Governance.
View fellowships
RELATED OPPORTUNITY

AI Existential Safety Community: A community dedicated to ensuring AI is developed safely, including both faculty and AI researchers. Members are invited to attend meetings, participate in an online community, and apply for travel support.

We do not accept unsolicited requests. Please subscribe to our newsletter and follow us on social media to learn more about our upcoming RFPs and Contests. Any questions about grants can be sent to grants@fut

Request for proposals on extreme power concentration

This request for proposals is closed. We stopped accepting applications after the deadline of July 2, 2026, and are no longer taking submissions. For questions about a proposal you have already submitted, email power-rfp@longview.org.

Longview Philanthropy is looking to fund proposals to better understand and reduce the risk of AI enabling the extreme concentration of power—the possibility that AI will enable a small group of people to gain durable control over the lives of everyone else.

We are funding work across two tracks:

Grants for projects, programs, new teams, and new organizations across twelve priority areas (listed below). We expect typical grants to initially be between $100K and $2M/yr, covering 6 to 18 months, but we will consider proposals outside this range when the work justifies it, and larger renewals are possible once there is evidence of success.
Career funding for individuals developing or transitioning skills into the area, including course buy-outs, post-docs, training, independent study, transition stipends, and relevant expenses.

You can apply for Grants here, and Career Funding here. The application deadline for both tracks was July 2, 2026. This round is now closed and we are no longer accepting applications.

### Verified Grant Opportunities (One-for-One Matching Table)

#### 1. Transformative AI Fund (TAIF)
- **Funding Organization:** Effective Altruism Funds
- **Open Browser Tab:** Tab 1
- **Research Topic / Focus Area:** Reducing global catastrophic and existential risks from advanced and transformative AI systems through technical AI safety research, formal verification, policy analysis, forecasting, training, and field infrastructure.
- **Award Size:** Typically $10,000 – $150,000 (rarely exceeding $300,000)
- **Application Deadline:** Rolling ("We are always open to applications")
- **Official URL:** https://funds.effectivealtruism.org/funds/transformative-ai

#### 2. The Corrigibility Research Fund
- **Funding Organization:** Lightcone Infrastructure Inc.
- **Open Browser Tab:** Tab 2
- **Research Topic / Focus Area:** Research advancing theoretical and empirical understanding of AI corrigibility—ensuring AI systems keep human principals informed and in control, actively facilitating the detection and correction of flaws in model thoughts, structure, and actions.
- **Award Size:** Typical grants: $5,000 – $35,000 (part of an active $200,000+ disbursement pool in 2026)
- **Application Deadline:** October 31, 2026 (Round 2)
- **Official URL:** https://corrigibilityresearch.org/

#### 3. Research Support Program
- **Funding Organization:** AI Alignment Foundation (AIAF)
- **Open Browser Tab:** Tab 3
- **Research Topic / Focus Area:** High-risk, high-reward R&D on alignment properties that persist and strengthen under recursive self-improvement; bringing non-traditional technical domains (cognitive neuroscience, mathematics, theoretical physics) into foundational alignment; paired with dedicated engineering execution teams.
- **Award Size:** Full project funding plus dedicated engineering teams to move concepts to published results
- **Application Deadline:** Rolling applications
- **Official URL:** https://www.aialignmentfoundation.org/approach/apply

#### 4. CLR Fund
- **Funding Organization:** Center on Long-Term Risk (CLR)
- **Open Browser Tab:** Tab 4
- **Research Topic / Focus Area:** Foundational AI alignment, game theory, multi-agent conflict-cooperation dynamics, and reducing risks of severe astronomical suffering (s-risks) from advanced artificial intelligence. Fully open to academic institutions and university researchers (with university indirect costs capped at 10%).
- **Award Size:** Customized per proposal (supports individual academic researchers, stipends, and project grants)
- **Application Deadline:** Rolling applications
- **Official URL:** https://longtermrisk.org/grantmaking/

#### 5. Open Call for Research Projects ("Fund Your Bet")
- **Funding Organization:** Iliad
- **Open Browser Tab:** Tab 5
- **Research Topic / Focus Area:** Theory-driven, mathematically founded research in foundational AI alignment connecting theoretical proofs with empirical observables, alongside methodologically mature, predictive experiments.
- **Award Size:** Project and seed funding for incubated research groups/labs (sized to project scope)
- **Application Deadline:** Rolling applications
- **Official URL:** https://www.iliad.ac/opportunity/open-call-fund-your-bet

#### 6. AI Safety & Externalities Research Fund
- **Funding Organization:** Paradigm 3
- **Open Browser Tab:** Tab 6
- **Research Topic / Focus Area:** Technical alignment questions, "guardian angel" models (custom-aligned to individual users), the "virtue vs. rules" divide in AI safety, generalization gap dynamics, benchmark unhobbling, and quantifying societal externalities of advanced AI systems.
- **Award Size:** Unspecified on page (proposals evaluated via direct submission to hi@paradigm3.org based on proposed budget)
- **Application Deadline:** Rolling applications
- **Official URL:** https://www.paradigm3.org/research/fund

#### 7. AI for Science & Safety Nodes RFP
- **Funding Organization:** Foresight Institute (in collaboration with the Cape Institute for Safe AI)
- **Open Browser Tab:** Tab 7
- **Research Topic / Focus Area:** Decentralized, open AI safety and science progress across three tracks: Track I: Local Compute (cryptographically owned/governed infrastructure), Track II: Coordination and Accountability (monitoring, verification, and alignment), and Track III: AI-first Science (Bio, Neuro, Nano safety).
- **Award Size:** Typically $30,000 – $100,000 (larger grants considered) + physical office space in San Francisco, Berlin, or Cape Town + private compute cluster access
- **Application Deadline:** October 31, 2026
- **Official URL:** https://foresight.org/grants/ai-science-safety-nodes-rfp/

#### 8. Project Tailwind
- **Funding Organization:** Coefficient Giving (philanthropic funding vehicle partnering with major donors)
- **Open Browser Tab:** Tab 8
- **Research Topic / Focus Area:** Ambitious, large-scale technical initiatives, independent research organizations, and foundational solutions addressing critical unsolved bottlenecks in AI safety and catastrophic risk mitigation.
- **Award Size:** Pre-seed: $200,000 – $2,000,000 | Seed: $2,000,000 – $20,000,000 | Scale: $20,000,000 – $200,000,000
- **Application Deadline:** Rolling applications
- **Official URL:** https://coefficientgiving.org/tailwind/

#### 9. Capacity-Building for Transformative AI Risks
- **Funding Organization:** Coefficient Giving
- **Open Browser Tab:** Tab 9
- **Research Topic / Focus Area:** Initiatives and programs that build research talent and infrastructure to address risks from transformative AI, including academic research fellowships, university curriculum development, technical training workshops, and pipeline transition programs.
- **Award Size:** Flexible grant sizes based on budget proposal
- **Application Deadline:** Rolling applications
- **Official URL:** https://coefficientgiving.org/funds/navigating-transformative-ai/funding-for-work-that-builds-capacity-to-address-risks-from-transformative-ai/

#### 10. 2026 Request for Proposals (ReLU Networks & Epistemic Standards)
- **Funding Organization:** Iliad
- **Open Browser Tab:** Tab 10
- **Research Topic / Focus Area:** Two targeted technical tracks: 1) Mathematically grounded theory on ReLU networks (loss-landscape geometry, learning coefficients, simplicity bias, singularities, fibers), and 2) Raising the epistemic bar of AI safety (red-teaming seminal safety results, adversarial collaborations, critical reviews, replication studies).
- **Award Size:** Multi-tier funding for incubated research organizations and academic teams
- **Application Deadline:** Rolling / Open Call
- **Official URL:** https://www.iliad.ac/opportunity/2026-request-for-proposals

#### 11. Rapid Grants

- **Open Browser Tab:** Tab 11

- **Award Size:** Up to $20,000 (Average decision turnaround: 4 days)
- **Application Deadline:** Rolling applications
- **Official URL:** https://bluedot.org/grants/rapid

- **Funding Organization:** Advanced Research + Invention Agency (ARIA) [UK Government]
- **Open Browser Tab:** Tab 12
- **Research Topic / Focus Area:** Leveraging AI-enabled formal methods and machine-checked mathematical proofs to model, analyze, and verify critical cyber and cyber-physical systems; funding Blue Teams to build production-grade, security-critical software components with verifiable safety properties stress-tested by red teams.
- **Award Size:** Approximately £2,500,000 – £3,500,000 per Blue Team (Total call £20,000,000 within a £59,000,000 programme)
- **Application Deadline:** Rolling applications (Next quarterly batch review cut-off: October 31, 2026, 14:00 GMT)
- **Official URL:** https://aria.org.uk/opportunity-spaces/trust-everything-everywhere/safeguarded-ai/funding

#### 13. Scaling Trust: Tracks 2 & 3 (Tooling & Fundamental Research)
- **Funding Organization:** Advanced Research + Invention Agency (ARIA) [UK Government]
- **Open Browser Tab:** Tab 13
- **Research Topic / Focus Area:** Building tools and theoretical foundations for AI agents to securely coordinate, negotiate, and verify with one another in untrusted multi-agent environments; includes Track 2 (open-source verifiable agent tooling) and Track 3 (foundational research across Formal AI Security, cyber-physical primitives, generative security, and 3 long-term UK Research Centres).
- **Award Size:** Component of £49,800,000 programme; includes major centre funding and multi-year project grants
- **Application Deadline:** Rolling applications (Next quarterly batch review cut-off: October 31, 2026, 14:00 GMT)
- **Official URL:** https://aria.org.uk/opportunity-spaces/trust-everything-everywhere/scaling-trust/funding

#### 14. Mathematical Foundations of Artificial Intelligence (MFAI) [NSF 24-569]
- **Funding Organization:** National Science Foundation (NSF) [US Government]
- **Open Browser Tab:** Tab 14
- **Research Topic / Focus Area:** Interdisciplinary collaborations between mathematicians, statisticians, computer scientists, and engineers to develop innovative, principled design and analysis approaches for AI technology; understanding theoretical boundaries, explainability, and forestalling unintended societal consequences.
- **Award Size:** Up to $8,500,000 per year (anticipated ~15 awards annually, typically ~$500,000 – $800,000+ each)
- **Application Deadline:** October 9, 2026 (Full Proposal Deadline)
- **Official URL:** https://www.nsf.gov/funding/opportunities/mfai-mathematical-foundations-artificial-intelligence

#### 15. Security, Privacy, and Trust in Cyberspace (SaTC 2.0) [NSF 25-515]
- **Funding Organization:** National Science Foundation (NSF) [US Government]
- **Open Browser Tab:** Tab 15
- **Research Topic / Focus Area:** Fundamental research across computing and AI to create secure, resilient, and trustworthy global cyber systems; addressing vulnerabilities in machine learning models, adversarial manipulation, algorithmic bias, systemic trust, and privacy-preserving computation.
- **Award Size:** Approximately 75 awards annually (~$60,000,000 – $70,000,000 total annual program budget; up to $600,000 for Small/RES awards, up to $1,200,000+ for Medium awards)
- **Application Deadline:** September 28, 2026 (Annual Target Date) / January 25, 2027 / Proposals accepted continuously (rolling)
- **Official URL:** https://www.nsf.gov/funding/opportunities/satc-20-security-privacy-trust-cyberspace

#### 16. Career Transition Grants
- **Funding Organization:** BlueDot Impact
- **Open Browser Tab:** Tab 16
- **Research Topic / Focus Area:** Comprehensive personal and project funding to enable academic researchers, postdocs, and technical specialists to transition full-time into technical AI safety, alignment research, or frontier AI governance; funds research time, living stipends, compute, and substantial technical research outputs.
- **Award Size:** Up to $200,000 (Average decision turnaround: 20 days)
- **Application Deadline:** Rolling applications
- **Official URL:** https://bluedot.org/grants/career-transition

#### 17. Unlocking Dataset Value for AI-Enabled Scientific Discovery (AI Datasets) [NSF 26-512]
- **Funding Organization:** National Science Foundation (NSF) [US Government]
- **Open Browser Tab:** Tab 17
- **Research Topic / Focus Area:** Structuring, curating, certifying, and validating open scientific datasets to ensure reliable, verifiable, bias-resistant, and trustworthy AI-driven discovery across scientific disciplines.
- **Award Size:** 25 to 50 awards: Impact awards up to $2,000,000; Flagship awards up to $5,000,000; Planning awards up to $100,000
- **Application Deadline:** November 4, 2026 (Annual Deadline)
- **Official URL:** https://www.nsf.gov/funding/opportunities/ai-datasets-unlocking-dataset-value-ai-enabled-scientific-discovery

### Analysis of AI Safety Funding Patterns & Funder Archetypes

A comparative analysis of current funding sources for AI safety, alignment, and trustworthy machine learning reveals four prominent organizational archetypes, each with distinct priorities, award scales, and application cadences:

1. **Government Science and Advanced Research Agencies (e.g., US NSF, UK ARIA)**
   - **Characteristics & Scale:** Government programs deploy the largest individual awards and aggregate budgets—ranging from multi-million-pound team contracts (£2.5M–£3.5M per project at ARIA) to large directorate allocations ($60M–$70M annually under NSF SaTC and $8.5M annually under NSF MFAI).
   - **Research Focus:** Heavily weighted toward mathematically rigorous foundations, formal verification, provable guarantees, cyber-physical safety, and dataset integrity. They tend to frame safety around "trustworthy computing," "resilience," and "mathematical foundations" rather than existential AGI risk.
   - **Eligibility & Mechanics:** Highly structured, multi-month peer-review cycles favoring tenured and tenure-track university PIs, university departments, and multi-institution academic consortia, with fixed target dates or annual submission deadlines.

2. **Private Philanthropic Foundations & Philanthropic Capital Pools (e.g., Coefficient Giving / Open Philanthropy, EA Funds TAIF, Center on Long-Term Risk, Lightcone)**
   - **Characteristics & Scale:** Philanthropic foundations are the dominant funders explicitly dedicated to catastrophic and existential risks from frontier AI and artificial general intelligence. Funding ranges from agile $10k–$150k checks (TAIF) to massive institutional building checks ($200k–$20M+ via Project Tailwind).
   - **Research Focus:** Concentrated on technical alignment (mechanistic interpretability, scalable oversight, corrigibility, eliciting latent knowledge, agent foundations) and frontier AI governance.
   - **Eligibility & Mechanics:** Highly receptive to academic faculty, postdocs, and graduate students, often permitting low institutional overhead (e.g., CLR's 10% overhead cap). Most operate on a rolling application basis with rapid turnaround times compared to traditional federal agencies.

3. **Specialized Technical Nonprofits & Research Incubators (e.g., Iliad, AI Alignment Foundation, Foresight Institute)**
   - **Characteristics & Scale:** These organizations target neglected technical niches that federal funders rarely touch—such as ReLU loss-landscape geometry, singular learning theory, agent foundations, and multi-agent cooperative game theory. Awards generally range from $5,000 to $100,000+.
   - **Holistic Support Model:** Beyond direct financial grants, these groups provide non-monetary capital that academic researchers frequently lack: dedicated full-time engineering execution teams (AIAF), dedicated private GPU compute clusters, and co-located physical hubs/office nodes in San Francisco, Berlin, and Cape Town (Foresight Institute).

4. **Talent Pipeline & Career Accelerator Funds (e.g., BlueDot Impact)**
   - **Characteristics & Scale:** These programs specialize in agile, rapid-turnaround grants ($20k microgrants decided in ~4 days; career transition grants up to $200k decided in ~20 days).
   - **Strategic Role:** Designed to bridge the gap between traditional academic posts and full-time AI safety research. They allow university-based researchers, postdocs, and transitioning scientists to fund computing resources, travel, or dedicated research semesters without institutional friction.
